analysis.investment_thesis: Aarti Industries' net profit has collapsed 72% from ₹1,186 Cr in FY22 to ₹331 Cr in FY25 — a nine-year profit CAGR of just 2.4% — yet the stock trades at 43x earnings with a promoter holding below my minimum 50% threshold; this is a value trap dressed in specialty chemicals clothes. The China+1 capex cycle (₹1,300-1,400 Cr per year) is consuming cash without translating into return on capital, and I see no near-term catalyst to reverse this.
key_strengths: Diversified specialty chemical portfolio serving pharma, agrochemicals, dyes and pigments — some structural China+1 tailwind exists
OCF positive in all five years (₹519–1,319 Cr range) showing the underlying chemical business does generate cash
Revenue did grow from ₹3,006 Cr to ₹7,271 Cr over nine years — the top line is real even if profitability is absent
key_risks: Net profit in structural decline: FY22 ₹1,186 Cr → FY23 ₹545 Cr → FY24 ₹416 Cr → FY25 ₹331 Cr — and EBITDA trend is also contracting
ROE 6% and ROCE 6.3% — both deeply below cost of capital; the company is destroying economic value despite accounting profits
Finance costs have nearly trebled from ₹86 Cr (FY21) to ₹275 Cr (FY25) as debt-funded capex erodes margins further
red_flags: Promoter holding 42.14% — below my hard 50% minimum; management does not have adequate skin in the game
P/E of 43.1x on collapsing profits — severely and dangerously overvalued
EBITDA contracting trend despite 10.3% revenue CAGR — operational leverage working in reverse
Market cap ₹16,006 Cr — 16x above my sweet spot
D/E 0.70 — above 0.6 threshold with rising debt trajectory
analysis.detailed_analysis:
The core problem at Aarti Industries is a mismatch between capital deployment and capital returns. The company has been investing ₹1,165–1,386 Cr per year in capex (plus large CWIP of ₹1,596 Cr) but each rupee of new revenue is generating lower profits — the FY22 EBITDA of ₹1,687 Cr has shrunk to ₹986 Cr in FY25 even as revenue grew by ₹1,185 Cr. Something is deeply wrong with pricing power, product mix, or cost structure.

At 43x earnings on a business generating 6% ROE, investors are paying a premium for a story that is empirically not playing out. I need to see promoter holding cross 50%, ROE cross 15%, and a clear margin recovery for at least two consecutive years before I would revisit. Today, this is an AVOID.
